result.topic_en: The page derives a q-series (basic hypergeometric) expansion for the ratio of infinite products Π(-ab,x)Π(-ac,x)/(Π(-a,x)Π(-abc,x)) by comparing coefficients of powers of a.

(4). But the coeff$^t$. of $a^n$ in $\frac{\Pi(ac, x)}{\Pi(abc, x)}$ can be shewn
to be equal to $c^n . \frac{(b-1)(b-x) \cdots (b-x^{n-1})}{(1-x)(1-x^2) \cdots (1-x^n)}$. and hence
$\frac{\Pi(-ac, x)}{\Pi(-abc, x)} = \frac{\Pi(-a, x)}{\Pi(-ab, x)} + a . \frac{(1-b)(1-c)}{1-x} . \frac{\Pi(-ax, x)}{\Pi(-ab, x)}$
$+ a^2 . \frac{(1-b)(x-b)(1-c)(x-c)}{(1-x)(1-x^2)} . \frac{\Pi(-ax^2, x)}{\Pi(-ab, x)} + \cdots$
(5). That is $\frac{\Pi(-ab, x)\, \Pi(-ac, x)}{\Pi(-a, x)\, \Pi(-abc, x)}$
$= 1 + a . \frac{(1-b)(1-c)}{(1-x)(1-a)} + a^2 . \frac{(1-b)(x-b)(1-c)(x-c)}{(1-x)(1-x^2)(1-a)(1-ax)} + \cdots$
